<a id="architecture"></a>

## Architecture

THE SEAM ALREADY EXISTS AND IS THE WHOLE POINT. `IPijRecords` (apps/web/src/features/089-first-class-pij/server/pij-records.interface.ts) is the one process-spawning boundary in the 089 read path. The poller, the API routes and the rail all consume that interface and nothing below it. So this work adds a SECOND implementation beside the existing `CliPijRecords` and selects between them at construction. No consumer changes. No UI changes. If a consumer needs to change, the seam was wrong and that is a STOP-AND-ASK, not a patch.

Three units, written and tested in isolation:
  u1 rs-client      — transport only. Auth, key read, 401 -> single re-read, GET /v1/seats, POST /v1/state.
  u2 rs-records     — IPijRecords implemented over u1, plus the field mapping and the honest gaps.
  u3 rs-events      — the single /v1/events subscriber: cursor, reconnect, backoff, key re-read.

u1 is the frozen seam for u2 and u3: settle its interface BEFORE either starts. u2 and u3 never call fetch directly and never read daemon.key — if they do, the layering has failed.

REFERENCE, NOT DEPENDENCY: pij's own TS client at .pi/extensions/pij/adapters/daemon-http.ts has the shape (auth, key read, events pump, cursor reconnect). COPY THE SHAPE. Do NOT import pij's tree, do not add a dependency on it, do not vendor the file wholesale — it carries pij-side concerns chainglass has no business holding, and chainglass is a READER.

HARD CONSTRAINTS from the pij-rs owner (pij-still-weasel), non-negotiable:
  - Reader only. No /v1/register, /v1/send, /v1/adopt, no writes of any kind from chainglass.
  - Never read ~/.pij-rs/pij.sqlite. The HTTP surface is the contract.
  - ONE subscriber, never per-row fan-out. A 179-row x 8s fan-out has already killed this once.
  - Read daemon.key from disk every time it is needed; never cache it across a 401, never hardcode.
  - Default stays legacy. This branch does not flip PIJ_SOURCE.

THE GAPS ARE PART OF THE CONTRACT, not omissions to fill in later. pij-rs carries no watchdog, bindHealth or degraded, and (until req-0040) no role. These map to an EXPLICIT unavailable marker. Rendering blank is a defect: an empty watchdog cell reads as 'your watchdog is off', which is false in the dangerous direction. This repo shipped exactly that bug once already (65f524ea9) and the fix is on record. Do not synthesise, do not default, do not infer a role from anything.

=== AMENDMENT 1, ruling defects B/C/D from the coder ack (2026-09-02). These override anything above. ===

C — SELECTION IS PER-METHOD, NOT WHOLESALE. My original instruction (throw on tree/nodeShow/raw) was WRONG and the ack proved it with LSP: /api/pij/tree calls records.tree() twice and /api/pij/focus calls records.nodeShow() and records.tree(). Throwing there breaks two live routes, which contradicts this plan's own 'no consumer changes'. RULING: build a COMPOSITE records adapter. list() and state() come from rs; tree(), nodeShow() and raw() continue to delegate to the existing CliPijRecords. This is a fourth unit, u4 composite-records, and it is the thing selected at the construction site — never RsPijRecords directly. The cost is honest and bounded: tree/nodeShow still spawn a process, but PER REQUEST (a user opening focus), not per 8s tick forever, which is the defect this plan exists to remove. u2 therefore does NOT throw for those methods; it simply does not implement them.

D — THE GAP MARKER IS AN ADDITIVE FIELD, NOT A VALUE. The ack is right that `bindHealth?: string`, `degraded?: boolean` and `liveness?: string` cannot all carry one marker, and that an omitted value renders as the blank this plan forbids. RULING: add ONE additive field to the row — `rsUnavailable?: string[]` — listing the field names this source cannot supply. PijListRow is explicitly open (`[additive: string]: unknown`) so this widens no existing contract and changes no existing type. Populate it from the LIVE `pij-rs state <id>` `unsupported[]` array, not from my hand-written list: the ack found the live array names more gaps than I did (activity, lastEventAt, ageMs, failureReason, bindHealth, degraded, degradedReason, watchdog, daemon tick fields) and one I had missed entirely — rs `liveness: active` covers BOTH the TS `active` and `stale` cases, so it is a WEAKER claim wearing the same word. Record that weakening in rsUnavailable too. Tombstone stays a mapped FACT, not a gap. Rendering the marker in the rail is OUT OF SCOPE for this plan and is oq-0003; this plan's job is to make the absence machine-readable rather than invisible.

B — u3 NEEDS A SEAM AND DOES NOT HAVE ONE. The ack is correct: PijPollerService.start() schedules private tickFast/tickSlow and its public interface has no event-ingestion or records-refresh entry point, so an RsEventStream started beside it cannot update the fleet and cannot meet appear/disappear <= 2s. RULING: u3 does NOT start beside the poller. Add ONE public method to PijPollerService — `ingest(event: RsEvent): void` — which applies an event to the in-memory rows and emits the same coalesced fleet-delta the fast tick already emits, reusing the existing coalescing path (MAX_BROADCASTS_PER_FAST_TICK) rather than inventing a second broadcast route. u3 calls it. This is an ADDITIVE change to the poller's public interface and is now inside your fence. If applying an event turns out to need the private tick internals, STOP and tell me — that would mean the seam is wrong and it is my problem, not yours to work around.

E — COMPOSITION IS YOURS. My impl-guide said the prime composes while your done bar requires live bp rows that cannot run until composition exists. That is my contradiction, not an ambiguity for you to resolve. RULING: YOU compose and YOU run bp-0001..0008. Your fence widens to include the construction site in start-pij-poller.ts and the single additive method on pij-poller.service.ts. I review and merge. There is no PM on this plan, so the composer was always going to be whoever could prove the result, and that is you.

A — fixed: plan.dd.md and tasks.dd.md were stale because I rewrote the JSON and never re-ran `ddocs build`. Both regenerated. Good catch; you were right not to review against an empty document.

| rationale | One coder, three units in a single wave — NOT a fleet, and no PM. ## Composition

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| composer | prime |
| steps | No PM, so the prime composes. 1) Select the implementation at the ONE construction site: start-pij-poller.ts getPijPoller() currently calls createPijRecords({defaultCwd}); it becomes a choice on PIJ_SOURCE, default legacy, shaped like the existing pijPollerEnabled() env helper so both branches stay testable without mutating global state. 2) Wire the event stream beside the poller, started only when PIJ_SOURCE=rs. 3) `just fft` green with PIJ_SOURCE unset (bp-0008). 4) Then, and only then, run the live backpressure rows against the running daemon. |
| integration_proof | `just fft` green with PIJ_SOURCE unset (bp-0008), then the live rows run against the running pij-rs daemon in this order: bp-0001 (no child process spawned), bp-0002 (reader equals a direct /v1/seats read for the same id), bp-0003 (a seat appears within 2s), bp-0004 (a seat DISAPPEARS within 2s), bp-0005 (daemon restart resumes from cursor), bp-0006 (rotated key -&gt; exactly one re-read). Every one of these is a command with an exit status, not an assertion in a test file — the whole point is that a fixture cannot prove a reader tracks a live fleet. |

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| r1 | Coder mocks the 401 path instead of exercising it. Retired by bp-0006, which requires a real daemon and a scratch key file — a mocked 401 proves the branch exists, not that the daemon accepts what was re-read. |
| r2 | Coder proves the reader by only ever ADDING seats. Retired by bp-0004, the negative: a closed seat must leave the reader within the same 2s bound. A reader that never forgets passes every positive test. |
| r3 | Coder fills the gaps (watchdog/bindHealth/degraded/role) with defaults or blanks to make the rail look complete. Retired by bp-0007. This is the single most likely well-intentioned defect in this plan. |
| r4 | Coder reaches for pij's tree — imports daemon-http.ts or adds a dependency on the pij repo. Retired at review: chainglass must build with the pij repo absent. |
| r5 | Coder flips the default to rs because it is obviously better. Retired by bp-0008 and by review: the flip is gated on plan-129 and req-0040, neither owned by this repo. |
| r6 | Per-row fan-out reappears as 'one request per seat' inside list(). Retired at review against the ONE-subscriber constraint; this pattern has already caused a fleet incident. |
